chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Abdullah said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who is hunting; he said, 'If he is circling around it, he should not shorten [the prayer], and if he is passing by the time, he should shorten [the prayer].'

key_terms.يُجَاوِزُ الْوَقْتَ: passes by the time (moving through the prayer time)

ai.seo_question: When should a hunting traveler shorten their prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the practical application of *Qasr* (shortening prayer) for a traveler engaged in hunting, distinguishing between stationary and mobile states. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that the status of 'traveler' (*musafir*) is determined by physical movement and distance from the city, rather than merely the intent to travel. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Islamic law in accommodating occupational activities while maintaining ritual obligations.
